chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a slave owned by partners, if one of them sells his share, the other partner says, 'I have more right to it.' Is that so? He said, 'Yes, if there is only one [other partner].' It was said to him, 'Is there shuf'ah in animals?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal to buy a partner's share)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of shuf'ah (pre-emption) for co-owned slaves and animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the scope of *shuf'ah* (pre-emption), affirming a co-owner's right to buy out a selling partner's share in a slave to preserve joint ownership. It notably restricts this right to cases with only one other partner and explicitly excludes animals, reflecting the juristic distinction between human and animal property in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the principle of preventing unwanted intrusion into shared assets while maintaining practical clarity in transactional disputes.
